model: IF-Module BACnet / IF-Module BACnet Stratos (BACnet MS/TP)
applies_to: Wilo IF-Module BACnet (2097811, glanded pumps such as IL-E/IP-E/DL-E/BL-E and MVIE/MHIE) and IF-Module BACnet Stratos (2097810, Stratos/Stratos-D/-Z), the plug-in modules that put older Wilo electronic pumps on BACnet MS/TP.
summary: The IF-Module BACnet plugs into older Wilo electronic pumps and makes the pump a BACnet MS/TP device (master from module software 2.00, slave if the MAC address is 128 or higher). Wilo's functional description gives one fixed object list of 57 objects: pump measurements, the bus setpoint and control-mode command, on/off and override commands, status bits, and the error and bus-command-timer objects. Each object is marked with the pump families that support it.
firmware: IF-Module BACnet 1.11 or later (some objects 2.00 or later)
notes: Taken from the BACnet object descriptions (section 6.2) in Wilo's IF-Module functional description; object type comes from the section heading (Analog Inputs, Analog Outputs, Binary Inputs, Binary Outputs, Multistate Inputs, Multistate Outputs).

Wilo marks each object with the pump families that support it (Stratos, IL-E family, MVIE family). Where an object is not supported by all three, the description names the families; 'Provided by the module' means the IF-Module itself supplies it.
Access: inputs (AI, BI, MI) are read-only; outputs (AO, BO, MO) are commandable, each printed with a relinquish default.
Multistate state texts list only the first word of each state; several states are marked reserved or valid only for some pump families.

integration.summary: Write BO 0 Bus Command Pump on and AO 0 Bus Setpoint, choose the control mode with MO 0, and keep the Bus Command Timer (MO 1) active so the pump stays under bus control. Read BI 10 Pump is operating, speed, power and the warning/error status bits, with MI 1 for the current error code.

minimum_points.name: Bus Command Timer
minimum_points.why: Write SET (2) before each timeout to keep bus control

integration.enable: MO 1 Bus Command Timer decides who controls the pump: MANUAL (the relinquish default) lets the pump menu and the bus both write, last write wins; SET locks the local menu for the timeout; OFF blocks local operation permanently. Commands then follow a fixed priority: Ext. off input at the pump, Override off, Override max, Override min, Override on.
integration.heartbeat: With MO 1 = SET the BMS must write SET again before the Bus Command Timer timeout (AO 8, default 300 s, module SW 2.00+). When it lapses the state goes to RESET: local operation is possible again and bus writes are blocked. Use SET_PRESET instead to load the preset values (AO 100, BO 100, MO 100, MO 101) on bus failure. MI 2 shows the timer state.
setup: The module is MS/TP master from module software 2.00; a MAC address of 128 or higher makes it an MS/TP slave. Baud rates 9600-115200.
The device instance is set with the pump menu parameters C, E and F (instance split as hex digits, per the IF-Module manual).
gotchas: Some commandable outputs use a floating default: the module writes it virtually at priority 16, so relinquishing all priorities does not always return the static relinquish default.
At double pumps fit the IF-Module in the master pump and use the integrated double-pump management.
